title: Any h sheaf turns an almost blowup square into a cartesian diagram of sets
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For a sheaf F on one of the big h sites and any almost blowup square in that category, the lemma asserts that the resulting square with entries F(E), F(X'), F(Z) and F(X) is cartesian in the category of sets (statement lines 11215-11228). The proof does not test the sheaf condition directly but substitutes a covering: since Z coproduct X' -> X is a surjective proper morphism of finite presentation, the singleton family is an h covering, and the sheaf condition for it computes F(X) as the equalizer of the two maps to F(Z coprod X') (proof lines 11231-11233). The author then expands the fibre product (Z coprod X') x_X (Z coprod X') = Z coprod E coprod E coprod (X' x_X X'), uses that a Zariski sheaf sends disjoint unions to products, and rewrites the sheaf condition concretely as: pairs (t, s') with t|_E = s'|_E and s' in the equalizer of the two maps F(X') -> F(X' x_X X') (proof lines 11234-11246). The remaining step removes condition (b) by observing that E x_Z E coprod X' -> X' x_X X' is again a surjective proper morphism of finite presentation, because b is an isomorphism away from E, so F(X' x_X X') -> F(E x_Z E) x F(X') is injective and (a) implies (b) (proof lines 11247-11255). Choosing the covering Z coproduct X' and then eliminating the second sheaf condition is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
